result.topic_en: The page shows how to derive new solutions of quadratic Diophantine equations of the form ax^2+by^2=cz^2 from one known solution, in fragments by Krafft, J. A. Euler and N. Fuss.
result.transcription:
206 L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA. Arithmetica.
$x = f(anpp - \beta nqq) - 2\beta ngpq, \quad y = g(anpp - \beta nqq) + 2anfpq.$
Videamus igitur an esse possit $n = \frac{1}{h}$, manentibus $x$ et $y$ integris. Cum igitur sit
$x = \frac{f(\alpha pp - \beta qq) - 2\beta gpq}{h}, \quad y = \frac{g(\alpha pp - \beta qq) + 2\alpha fpq}{h},$
quod evenit si $p$ et $q$ ita sumantur, ut $fq + gp$ fiat per $h$ divisibile.
(W. L. Krafft.)
Problematis supra propositi solutio facillime sequenti modo absolvetur, siquidem constet unus casus, quo sit $\alpha ff + \beta gg = \gamma hh$, ubi scilicet $x = f$, $y = g$ et $z = h$. Statuamus $x = fp + \beta gq$ et $y = gp - \alpha fq$, tum enim erit
$\alpha xx + \beta yy = pp(\alpha ff + \beta gg) + \alpha\beta qq(\alpha ff + \beta gg) = \gamma hh(pp + \alpha\beta qq).$
Sicque aequatio adhuc resolvenda erit $hh(pp + \alpha\beta qq) = zz$, ita ut $pp + \alpha\beta qq$ debeat reddi quadratum, quod fit capiendo $p = rr - \alpha\beta ss$ et $q = 2rs$, tum enim fit
$pp + \alpha\beta qq = (rr + \alpha\beta ss)^2.$
Ideoque $z = h(rr + \alpha\beta ss)$. Ipsarum vero $x$ et $y$ valores erunt
$x = f(rr - \alpha\beta ss) + 2\beta grs, \quad y = g(rr - \alpha\beta ss) - 2\alpha frs,$
ubi numeri $r$ et $s$ pro lubitu assumi possunt. (Conf. Comment. arithm. T. I. p. 556.)
A. m. T. I. p. 95. 96. 98. 99.

40.
(J. A. Euler.)
Theorema. Si fuerint $naa + pbb = \square = cc$ et $nff + qgg = \square = hh$, tum semper assignare licet $x$ et $y$, ut sit $nxx + pqyy = \square = zz$.
Demonstratio. Cum sit $pbb = cc - naa$ et $qgg = hh - nff$, erit productum
$pqbbgg = (cc - naa)(hh - nff) = (ch + naf)^2 - n(ah + fc)^2,$
unde manifestum est fore $n(ah + fc)^2 + pqbbgg = (ch + naf)^2$, sicque erit
$x = ah + fc, \quad y = bg \quad \text{et} \quad z = ch + naf.$
A. m. T. I. p. 130

41.
(N. Fuss I.)
Problema. Resolvere aequationem $\lambda zz = \mu xx + \nu yy$, ex cognito casu $\lambda cc = \mu aa + \nu bb$.
Solutio. A priore aequatione in $cc$ ducta subtrahatur posterior in $zz$ ducta, eritque
$0 = \mu(ccxx - aazz) + \nu(ccyy - bbzz),$
sive $\mu(ccxx - aazz) = \nu(bbzz - ccyy)$, hinc $\frac{\mu(cx + az)}{bz - cy} = \frac{\nu(bz + cy)}{cx - az}.$
Utraque haec fractio statuatur $= \frac{p}{q}$ et ex priore elicitur
$z = \frac{\mu cqx + pcy}{bp - \mu aq}$ et ex altera $z = \frac{cpx - \nu cqy}{\nu bq + ap}$,
qui duo valores inter se aequati dant
$\frac{y}{x} = \frac{\mu\nu bcqq + 2\mu acpq - bcpp}{\mu\nu acqq - 2\nu bcpq - acpp}.$
Statuatur ergo $x = \mu\nu aqq - 2\nu bpq - app$ et $y = \mu\nu bqq + 2\mu apq - bpp$,
sive $x = a(\mu\nu qq - pp) - 2\nu bpq$ et $y = b(\mu\nu qq - pp) + 2\mu apq$.

items.quote: Videamus igitur an esse possit $n = \frac{1}{h}$, manentibus $x$ et $y$ integris.
items.english: Let us therefore see whether it can be that n = 1/h, with x and y remaining integers.

items.quote: Problematis supra propositi solutio facillime sequenti modo absolvetur, siquidem constet unus casus, quo sit $\alpha ff + \beta gg = \gamma hh$
items.english: The solution of the problem proposed above is most easily accomplished in the following way, provided one case is known in which αff + βgg = γhh.

items.quote: Theorema. Si fuerint $naa + pbb = \square = cc$ et $nff + qgg = \square = hh$, tum semper assignare licet $x$ et $y$, ut sit $nxx + pqyy = \square = zz$.
items.english: Theorem. If naa + pbb = a square = cc and nff + qgg = a square = hh, then one can always assign x and y so that nxx + pqyy = a square = zz.

items.quote: Problema. Resolvere aequationem $\lambda zz = \mu xx + \nu yy$, ex cognito casu $\lambda cc = \mu aa + \nu bb$.
items.english: Problem. To solve the equation λzz = μxx + νyy, from the known case λcc = μaa + νbb.
